Americans Went Berserk Wishing Socialism and a Social State 🇺🇸


Polls have shown that more people than ever have a negative view of the tech, and you can take your pick on the reasons why. 

AI could displace jobs, destroy the environment, and drive up energy bills. It’s trained on stolen writing and artwork, and chatbots are driving people into mental health spirals.

But what does the public think should be done about this? A new national survey from Versasight suggests that the majority of Americans are down for taking a drastic course of action.

According to the survey of 9,700 adults, an impressive 79 percent of US employees support forcing AI companies to transfer 50 percent of their stock into a public wealth fund, an idea that has been championed by senator Bernie Sanders (D-VT).

“In the eyes of the public, AI Sovereign funds are seen as a tool to distribute the gains from the AI industry back to broader society,”
 Verasight CEO Benjamin Leff told CNBC News. 

Once at the fringe of political discourse, Sanders took the idea mainstream when he proposed the American AI Sovereign Wealth Fund Act in June. In an essay published in the New York Times, the independent senator argued that the creation of this fund would “give the public a direct role in determining the future of this technology.”

“It would guarantee that the economic benefits generated by AI are used to improve the lives of all of us — not simply to make the richest people in the world even richer,”
 he added in a statement last month.

The act would target the largest AI companies in the US such as Anthropic and OpenAI, mandating that they submit to a one time 50 percent tax on their stock. At their current valuations, Sanders estimated that this would create a fund worth around $7 trillion. 

The money in this fund could offset some of the widespread disruption AI could wreak on society, the thinking goes.

Not all AI industry critics are on board. Some have argued that giving the government such a large stake in AI companies would encourage it to clear away regulations, and give AI companies even greater influence over the government than they already have.

You could say it’s a flawed and far-fetched idea, but Americans are on board, perhaps underscoring the desperation for someone to do something about the industry. Even when the policy was explicitly tied to Sanders, the survey found that 64 percent of respondents still supported the idea.

“There is an undeniable desire among Americans of both parties for federal oversight, absolute transparency, and accountability to ensure AI safety and to enable all Americans to participate in the economic benefits of AI,”
 Leff said in a statement.

❗️ What is the Coinbase Premium Index? U.S. Bitcoin demand gauge 

➡️ One number tells you whether United States institutions are buying Bitcoin or backing away: the gap between the price on Coinbase and the price on the rest of the world’s exchanges. Here is how the Coinbase Premium Index works, why it moved markets in 2026, and how to read it without fooling yourself.

⚠️ Every market has a tell. In Bitcoin, one of the most watched is almost embarrassingly simple: the same coin trades on hundreds of venues at once, and the price is never exactly the same everywhere. Most of those gaps are noise. One of them is a signal, because of who trades where.

🔖 Coinbase is the exchange of record for regulated American money. Hedge funds, corporate treasuries, registered advisors, and, most importantly, the custodial and trading infrastructure behind the United States spot Bitcoin ETFs all route disproportionately through it. Binance and the other global venues carry everyone else. When Bitcoin trades richer on Coinbase than on the global market, someone in the American regulated system is paying up to buy. When it trades cheaper, that bid is gone, or has turned into supply.

⚡️ Scientific, technological cooperation key to Iran-Iraq strategic ties: Minister

📌 Tehran, IRNA – Minister of Information and Communications Technology, Sattar Hashemi, has emphasized Iran’s readiness to share expertise in electronic health, space technology, and communications research, calling scientific and technological cooperation the cornerstone for broader strategic ties between Tehran and Baghdad.

Hashemi met with Abdul Hussein al-Moussawi, the Iraqi Health Minister and the Acting Minister of Higher Education and Scientific Research, on Wednesday.
​
During the meeting, the two officials emphasized that enhancing scientific and technological cooperation is a top priority for the two countries.
​
Referring to the deep historical and cultural bonds, the two sides considered these commonalities a suitable platform for expanding interactions in new fields of knowledge and technology.
​
Highlighting the capabilities and advancements of the Islamic Republic in the space industry, Hashemi said, “In recent years, Iran has made significant progress in telecommunications and remote sensing satellites and is prepared to enhance these capabilities within the framework of joint cooperation with Iraq”.
​
He also cited the establishment of a joint research and development center, cooperation in satellite imagery, development of ground stations, and expansion of cooperation in the space industry as key areas of collaboration between the two countries.
​
For his part, Al-Moussawi emphasized the importance of Iran’s experiences in health, education, and technology, highlighting the Iraqi government’s commitment to fostering and enhancing scientific and technological relations with the Islamic Republic of Iran.

📄 Attack on Dena destroyer exposes enemy fear of Iran’s naval power: Senior commander

📌 Tehran, IRNA – The Deputy Commander of the Islamic Republic of Iran’s Navy, Rear Admiral Faramarz Bemani, says the attack on the Dena destroyer exposed the enemy’s fear of Iran’s growing naval capabilities and international standing.

“Targeting of the Dena destroyer is a testament to the enemy’s fear of Iran’s naval power and its achievements on the international stage, because this destroyer is a symbol of indigenous capability, self-belief, and the will of the Iranian people,” Bemani said Wednesday at the 27th basic combat training course for national elites, held at Army Ground Forces Martyrs Training Center in Tehran.
​
“Dena destroyer and port vessel Makran, by circumnavigating the globe, demonstrated the naval power of the Islamic Republic of Iran and, despite sanctions, conveyed Iran’s message of peace, capability, and independence to the world,” he said.
​
He described the mission of Naval Fleet 86 as one of Iran’s greatest sources of pride.
​
The deputy commander emphasized that enemies target the strong points of the Islamic Republic, and the targeting of the Dena destroyer indicates the enemy’s fear of Iran’s maritime power and its achievements internationally.
​
Turning to the role of youth, he said their contribution to the Revolution’s goals was central.
​
He outlined the Navy’s history from ancient Iranian seafaring traditions to its current mandate, noting it now guards territorial waters, the Sea of Oman, the Indian Ocean, and the Caspian Sea in coordination with the Islamic Revolution Guards Corps Navy.
​
He said that during the first 67 days of the eight-year imposed war, the Army Navy destroyed much of the Iraqi Ba’athist regime’s naval capacity and went on to escort thousands of commercial vessels and oil tankers to prevent economic disruption.
​
Bemani said Iran today is among a small number of countries capable of independently designing and building destroyers, missiles, drones, and advanced naval equipment, the result of work by domestic specialists, universities, and knowledge-based companies.
​
Closing his remarks, Bemani invited elites to join the Navy’s scientific and defense development path.
​
“The future of Iran will be built by elite youth, and the Army Navy welcomes their scientific and research capacity for developing new technologies and strengthening the country’s defense capabilities,” he said.
​
The Navy participated in the Armed Forces Achievements Exhibition for conscript elites with 14 booths, displaying research projects and technologies including electronic warfare systems, phased-array radars, radar-evading composite equipment, drone and quadcopter systems, training simulators, and water purification equipment.
